subject: Operational readout: Aurora Health incident, SLA deviation & action tracker
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Leadership Team <leadership@redwood.ai>; SRE Pager <sre@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Operational readout: Aurora Health incident, SLA deviation & action tracker

Team,

Summary (short): On 2026-10-01 22:45 UTC we observed sustained request queue growth on the inference fleet serving Aurora Health (AH-3342). Impact window: ~22:45–23:55 UTC — elevated latencies and 5xx spike caused ~12 minutes of degraded throughput and a longer SLA deviation window for scheduled batch jobs. Root cause (preliminary): cache eviction pathology plus an autoscaler race under a burst workload from a recurring cron job.

What I attached:
- aurora-postmortem-20261002.pdf (full timeline, root cause analysis, mitigations)
- sla-deviation-heatmap-20261002.csv (per-route token-level latency and error rates)
- action-items-aurora-20261004.gsheet (working tracker with owners & ETA)

Immediate asks for leadership:
1) Review the attached exec summary and confirm priority for a formal credit decision (procurement is asking for an SLA credit estimate).
2) Confirm resource priority for the 48-hour hotfix (Marcus + SRE + Infra); preliminary estimate: 1.5 engineer-weeks and a config rollout window.
3) For QBR: I want to include a brief (<=3 slide) slide showing incident, root cause, permanent mitigation plan, and committed timelines.

Action items I’ve already assigned in the sheet:
- Marcus Lin: produce a safe autoscaler gating patch (ETA 2026-10-06)
- Laura Bennett: customer comms + credit runbook & procurement liaison (ETA 2026-10-05)
- Vivek: approve executive talking points and sign-off on any customer credits (ETA 2026-10-04 EOD)

I’ll take point on the QBR slide and the executive narrative. Please reply with concerns or changes to owners.

-Markus
Director of Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

[attachment: aurora-postmortem-20261002.pdf] [attachment: sla-deviation-heatmap-20261002.csv] [link: action-items-aurora-20261004.gsheet]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operational readout: Aurora Health incident, SLA deviation & action tracker

Thanks Markus — review notes below. Good work aggregating the timeline. Two quick asks before I sign off on the customer comms: 

1) Executive numbers: please call out the precise SLA metric deviation and proposed credit range (e.g., 2.5% credit vs. 5% vs. full-month prorate). I need the projected cost impact line.
2) Risk to other top-tier accounts: is this localized to the Aurora workload shape (cron burst) or do we have evidence other customers saw similar flares? If localized, call that out.

I’ll be available for a 30-min sync at 11:00 PT if helpful.

-Vivek
CTO, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 11:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operational readout: Aurora Health incident, SLA deviation & action tracker

Adding context from customer ops and procurement side.

- Procurement has already pinged for an initial credit estimate (Procurement <procurement@aurorahealth.com>). They asked for a formal number by COB Monday (2026-10-05).
- Customer impact: Aurora reports delayed clinical report generation for a few customers; they categorize this as "operational disruption" not critical patient safety, but resolution time matters for renewal conversations.

I updated the action-items sheet with more granular fields: severity, upstream owner, verification step, rollback plan. Short highlights: 
- Credit calc: finance estimates ~3.1% revenue exposure for the incident window if we offer a token/time-proportional credit; I put a tentative band 2–4% in the sheet.
- Comms plan: initial "we are investigating" note sent; proposed F/U tomorrow with root cause and next steps.

Marcus — can you confirm the timeboxed patch plan and whether a canary rollout is sufficient? Also adding Evelyn for any exec comms/library items for QBR.

-Laura
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

[attachment: sla-deviation-heatmap-20261002.csv]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, SRE Pager <sre@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 14:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operational readout: Aurora Health incident, SLA deviation & action tracker

Laura — quick technical note. Summary of plan:
- Short term: implement autoscaler gating and reduce aggressive default max-in-flight for scheduled jobs. Canary rollout tomorrow night (2026-10-03 02:00–05:00 UTC), monitor queue length + 95th percentile latency.
- Medium term: introduce a shedding policy for cron-driven bursts and refine KV cache TTL heuristics (ETA 2026-10-18).
- Verification: I’ll post canary metrics in the action tracker and set an SLO alert threshold for automated rollback.

If we confirm the canary window is acceptable, I’ll coordinate with SRE to reserve capacity and set monitoring dashboards.

-Marcus
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

> On Fri, Oct 2, 2026 at 11:15 AM Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai> wrote:
> > Marcus — can you confirm the timeboxed patch plan and whether a canary rollout is sufficient?

From: Ben Jacobs <ben.jacobs@aurorahealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operational readout: Aurora Health incident, SLA deviation & action tracker

Hi Laura / Markus,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the timeline. A couple of items from our side: 
- Procurement is asking for a written credit estimate and the timeline for mitigation before next Tuesday (2026-10-06).
- Our engineering lead would like confirmation that the fix will be canaried and not rolled to all production at once. We cannot risk a wider disruption during our end-of-quarter batch processing on 2026-10-07.

Please include an estimated credit percentage and a clear canary timeline in the comms. If possible, include a note on steps you’ll take to prevent recurrence (we saw similar behavior late last quarter and want assurance this won’t recur).

Thanks,
Ben
Director, Platform Engineering
Aurora Health

[Procurement looped: procurement@aurorahealth.com]

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Jacobs <ben.jacobs@aurorahealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operational readout: Aurora Health incident, SLA deviation & action tracker

Ben — thanks for the clarity. Confirming next steps: 
- Credit estimate: we’ll propose a token/time-proportional credit in the 2–4% band; Laura will formalize the number after finance finalizes the calc on Monday.
- Canary: confirmed — we will canary the autoscaler gating patch in the scheduled window 2026-10-03 02:00–05:00 UTC. No immediate wide rollout.
- Communication: we’ll send a formal technical note post-canary with metrics and a remediation timeline.

I’ll follow up after the canary completes with outcomes. Apologies for the disruption and thanks for working with us.

-Markus

> On Sat, Oct 3, 2026 at 08:22 AM Ben Jacobs <ben.jacobs@aurorahealth.com> wrote:

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Leadership Team <leadership@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 4 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operational readout: Aurora Health incident, SLA deviation & action tracker — QBR inclusion

Folks — brief note for QBR framing.

- For the QBR slide deck: include one slide with 3 bullets — incident overview, RCA (1-liner), AFAs (actions, owners, ETA). Keep the slide consumable for execs (no more than ~120 words). Markus, please attach the 1-slide artifact by Monday COB so we can assemble the deck.
- I recommend we add a short "lessons learned" line: "Improve autoscaler gating and scheduled-job throttling; add per-tenant burst detection".
- If leadership signs the proposed credit band today, CS will prepare a tailored note for the customer to be delivered after the canary verification.

Evelyn
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
